title: What Did Ancient Humans Do All Day?
alternative_titles: Did Farming Make Us Work Harder?
description: A dry-run sample: how hunter-gatherers spent their days, and what farming changed.
main_character: a round-headed caveman with messy brown hair and a fur tunic

scenes.narration: Imagine a day with no clock and no boss. You wake when the sun warms the cave mouth. Breakfast is whatever was left from last night. And nobody is waiting for you to clock in.
scenes.visual_description: caveman stretching at a cave entrance at sunrise

scenes.narration: Anthropologists who timed hunter-gatherers found something surprising. Getting food took about seventeen hours a week. The rest of the time went to people.
scenes.visual_description: a scientist with a notebook and stopwatch sitting on a rock

scenes.narration: Then came farming. Fields needed weeding, watering and guarding from dawn to dusk. Skeletons from early farms show shorter, sicker people.
scenes.visual_description: tired caveman with a hoe in a wheat field, sweat drops flying

beats.picture: a row of small skeletons standing side by side

scenes.narration: So were our ancestors lazy, or were they rich in time? Tell me in the comments which life you would choose.
